subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: Should OpenClaw add a global agent tool-execution dry-run, and if so should Phase 1 be CLI-only or a run-scoped Gateway/embedded contract from the start?
rationale: This changes the core safety contract for all agent tools and needs maintainer intent on scope, concurrency, hook ordering, and redaction before automation can safely implement it.

options.title: Approve scoped CLI contract
options.body: Implement a CLI-visible, run-scoped dry-run preview that preserves policy hooks and redacts tool parameters before returning structured dry-run results.

options.title: Design Gateway-wide contract first
options.body: Pause implementation until Gateway, embedded, client-tool, and concurrency semantics are specified together.

options.title: Decline global dry-run
options.body: Keep command-specific dry-runs plus existing approvals and tool allowlists as the supported safety model.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped CLI contract
recommendation.body: Implement a CLI-visible, run-scoped dry-run preview that preserves policy hooks and redacts tool parameters before returning structured dry-run results.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant history shows repeated ownership of the agent CLI and tool adapter surfaces, and the decision spans those core paths.
